questions.q: Which holder is returned by `SELECT holder FROM policies WHERE status='Active' AND state='NY'`?
questions.why: Only C. Iyer is both Active and in NY.

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE product='Term Life' OR premium > 1400`?
questions.why: Two Term Life policies plus Whole Life (3400) and Auto (1500).

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE state='MA' OR state='NY' AND status='Lapsed'`?
questions.why: AND runs before OR, so this means MA rows OR (NY and Lapsed): 2 + 1. Use brackets to be safe.

questions.q: How many policies have `premium > 1000`?
questions.why: 1200, 3400 and 1500. The NULL premium is neither bigger nor smaller, so it drops out.

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE NOT status='Active'`?
questions.why: Lapsed and Pending.

days.title: Day 2 · Banking · IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, NULL

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE channel IN ('UPI','ATM')`?
questions.why: Three UPI and one ATM.

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE amount BETWEEN 700 AND 2500`?
questions.why: BETWEEN includes both ends: 2500, 700 and 1500.

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE channel <> 'UPI'`?
questions.why: NEFT and ATM. The NULL channel is not 'not UPI' to SQL. It is unknown, so it is excluded.

questions.q: How many rows: `WHERE txn_date LIKE '2026-01-0%'`?
questions.why: Dates 03, 05, 07 and 07. `%` matches any characters after.

questions.q: What does `COALESCE(channel,'BRANCH')` return for txn 5?
questions.why: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL value. Use it to label missing data in reports.

questions.q: `ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1` returns:
questions.why: OFFSET 1 skips the top row (Jeans), leaving the 2nd most expensive.

questions.q: How many rows: `SELECT DISTINCT dept, supplier FROM items`?
questions.why: DISTINCT works on the whole row (dept and supplier together). Grocery appears with S1, S2 and NULL.

questions.q: With `CASE WHEN price>=1000 THEN 'Premium' WHEN price>=400 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Value' END`, how many are 'Mid'?
questions.why: Rice (450) and Kettle (899). T-Shirt at 399 just misses. CASE stops at the first true branch.

questions.q: First row of `ORDER BY dept, price DESC`?
questions.why: Sorts by dept A→Z first (Apparel), then by price high→low within it.

questions.q: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT supplier) FROM items` returns:
questions.why: S1, S2, S3. NULL is not counted.

days.title: Day 4 · Health insurance claims · GROUP BY, HAVING

questions.q: `SELECT denial_reason, COUNT(*) FROM claims GROUP BY denial_reason ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1` returns which reason?
questions.why: NULLs form their own group, and 3 claims have no reason. Add `WHERE denial_reason IS NOT NULL` for the real top reason.

questions.q: Which providers survive `GROUP BY provider HAVING SUM(billed) > 2500`?
questions.why: City Hospital 10000, Care Clinic 2000, Lab One 600.

questions.q: `SELECT AVG(paid) FROM claims` returns:
questions.why: 5200 ÷ 5. The Pending claim's NULL is skipped, but the zero-paid denials are counted.

questions.q: Overall denial rate: `100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status='Denied' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)`
questions.why: 3 denied out of 6 claims. SUM(CASE…) is the standard way to count a condition.

questions.q: Why write `100.0 *` instead of `100 *` in a rate?
questions.why: In many databases 3/6 with whole numbers is 0. A decimal forces decimal maths.

days.title: Day 5 · Retail suppliers · INNER and LEFT JOIN

questions.q: How many rows: `items JOIN suppliers ON items.supplier = suppliers.supplier_id`?
questions.why: Soap has no supplier, so INNER JOIN drops it.

questions.q: How many rows: `suppliers LEFT JOIN items ON ...`?
questions.why: S1→2 items, S2→1, S3→2, and HomeCo is kept once with NULLs.

questions.q: Which supplier is returned by `suppliers LEFT JOIN items ... WHERE items.item_id IS NULL`?
questions.why: The anti-join pattern: suppliers with zero items listed.

questions.q: `items LEFT JOIN suppliers ON ... WHERE suppliers.country='IN'` returns how many rows?
questions.why: Filtering the right table in WHERE throws away the NULL rows, so your LEFT JOIN behaves like an INNER JOIN. Put the condition in ON to keep all 6 items.

questions.q: How many rows: `items CROSS JOIN suppliers`?
questions.why: Every item with every supplier: 6 × 4.

days.title: Day 6 · Agile delivery · Self joins and metrics

questions.q: Using `people e LEFT JOIN people m ON e.manager_id = m.id`, who is Vik's manager?
questions.why: A self join reads one table twice: once as employees, once as managers.

questions.q: How many direct reports does Priya have?
questions.why: Arun and Neha. Vik reports to Arun, not Priya.

questions.q: Team Beta's predictability, `100.0 * SUM(done points) / SUM(all points)`:
questions.why: Beta finished 7 of its 10 points.

questions.q: Total points on epics owned by Neha (`stories JOIN epics JOIN people`)?
questions.why: Neha owns Policy Docs (8 + 5) and Claims API (3).

questions.q: Which epic has no Done stories? (`NOT EXISTS`)
questions.why: Claims API has only a carried-over story.

questions.q: How many accounts: `WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts)`?
questions.why: Average is 92,000. ACC2 and ACC4 are above it.

questions.q: How many accounts sit above their own branch average (correlated subquery)?
questions.why: ACC1 beats Chennai's 30,000 and ACC2 beats Mumbai's 140,000. ACC4 equals Delhi's average, which isn't above it.

questions.q: How many accounts appear in `(SELECT account FROM transactions WHERE type='CREDIT')`?
questions.why: ACC1 and ACC2.

questions.q: The watchlist holds 'ACC3' and a NULL. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts WHERE acc NOT IN (SELECT acc FROM watchlist)` returns:
questions.why: One NULL in a NOT IN list makes every comparison unknown, so the result is zero. A real production bug.

questions.q: Same question with `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM watchlist w WHERE w.acc = accounts.acc)`:
questions.why: NOT EXISTS ignores the NULL safely. Prefer it over NOT IN.

days.title: Day 8 · Product analytics · Funnels with CTEs

questions.q: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events WHERE event='kyc'`
questions.why: Includes user 5, who did KYC without signing up. Raw counts can overstate a funnel step.

questions.q: `WITH signed AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM events WHERE event='signup')` + users from `signed` who did KYC:
questions.why: Users 1, 2 and 4. The CTE keeps the funnel honest.

questions.q: Signup → activate conversion?
questions.why: 2 of 4 signed-up users activated.

questions.q: How many users signed up and activated on the same day?
questions.why: Only user 4, on day 2.

questions.q: How long does a CTE exist?
options: Only for the one statement it belongs to
questions.why: A CTE is a named subquery for a single statement. For reuse across queries, create a view.

days.title: Day 9 · Retail stores · Ranking with window functions

questions.q: Using `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY store ORDER BY revenue DESC)`, how many rows have number 1?
questions.why: One per store: Chennai, Mumbai and Delhi.

questions.q: Chennai months have revenue 120, 120 and 100. What do RANK and DENSE_RANK give the 100 month?
questions.why: RANK leaves a gap after a tie; DENSE_RANK doesn't.

questions.q: Which store ranks #1 by total revenue?
questions.why: Mumbai 600, Chennai 340, Delhi 90.

questions.q: How many rows does `SELECT store, SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY store) FROM store_sales` return?
questions.why: A window function adds a column without collapsing rows. GROUP BY would give 3.

questions.q: Mumbai month 3's share of Mumbai revenue: `100.0 * revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY store)`

days.title: Day 10 · Banking ledger · Running totals, LAG, LEAD

questions.q: ACC1's running balance after day 3: `SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY acc ORDER BY d)`
`LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY acc ORDER BY d)` for ACC1 on day 1:
questions.why: Day 1 has no previous row, so the result is NULL.

questions.q: ACC1's day-4 change: `amount - LAG(amount) OVER (...)`
`LEAD(d) OVER (PARTITION BY acc ORDER BY d)` for ACC2's day-1 row:
questions.why: ACC2's next entry is on day 3.

questions.q: ACC1's 3-entry moving sum on day 4: `ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`

days.title: Day 11 · Insurance renewals · Messy text and dates

questions.q: The state values are 'MA', 'MA ' and 'ma'. How many groups does `GROUP BY state` produce for them?
questions.why: Trailing spaces and case make them different values. `GROUP BY UPPER(TRIM(state))` gives 1.

questions.q: `SUBSTR('LIF-2031', 1, 3)` returns:
questions.why: Start at position 1 and take 3 characters. Handy for product codes.

questions.q: Dates stored as text 'DD-MM-YYYY': which comes first in `ORDER BY due`?
questions.why: Text sorts character by character, so '05' beats '20'. That's wrong, because Dec 2026 is earliest. Store dates as DATE or as ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

questions.q: `WHERE due BETWEEN '2026-12-01' AND '2026-12-31'`: how many December renewals are counted?
questions.why: '2026-12-31 10:00' is later than '2026-12-31', so it's missed. Use `due < '2027-01-01'` for timestamps.

questions.q: What does `NULLIF(0, 0)` return, and why is it used in `claims / NULLIF(policies, 0)`?
questions.why: NULLIF turns 0 into NULL, and dividing by NULL gives NULL instead of crashing.

days.title: Day 12 · Release planning · Set operations and query order

questions.q: PI-1 features: Login, Docs, Search. PI-2: Docs, Search, Chat, Search. How many rows from `UNION`?
questions.why: UNION removes duplicates: Login, Docs, Search, Chat.

questions.q: Same tables with `UNION ALL`?
questions.why: UNION ALL keeps everything: 3 + 4. It's also faster, because it skips de-duplication.

questions.q: `pi1 INTERSECT pi2` returns how many features?
questions.why: Docs and Search are in both. These are features carried across PIs.

questions.q: `pi1 EXCEPT pi2` returns:
questions.why: In PI-1 but dropped from PI-2. (Oracle calls this MINUS.)

questions.q: In what order does SQL logically run a query?
options: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY
questions.why: This explains why a SELECT alias can't be used in WHERE but can be used in ORDER BY.

days.title: Day 13 · Investing · A personal stock portfolio

questions.q: Realised profit on sold positions: `SUM((sell_price - buy_price) * shares) WHERE sell_price IS NOT NULL`
Market value of open positions: `portfolio JOIN prices`, `SUM(shares * close) WHERE sell_price IS NULL`
Which ticker is returned by `GROUP BY ticker HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`?
questions.why: BLK was bought twice, at different prices.

questions.q: BLK's weighted average buy price: `SUM(shares * buy_price) / SUM(shares)`
questions.why: (2 × 700 + 1 × 900) ÷ 3. Plain AVG(buy_price) gives 800 and ignores position size, a common reporting mistake.

questions.q: JPM unrealised gain: `100.0 * (close - buy_price) / buy_price`

days.title: Day 14 · Career moves · A job-application tracker

questions.q: How many applications are at stage 'Interview'?
questions.why: BlackRock and BCG.

questions.q: Which role holds the highest offer? (`ORDER BY offer_eur DESC LIMIT 1`)
questions.why: 105,000 beats 95,000. Careful: in some databases (PostgreSQL, Oracle) NULLs sort first in DESC, so add `WHERE offer_eur IS NOT NULL`.

questions.q: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT company) FROM applications`
questions.why: JPMorgan appears twice.

questions.q: Offer rate: `100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN stage='Offer' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)`
questions.why: 2 offers from 6 applications.

questions.q: Keeping only the latest application per company (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY company ORDER BY applied DESC) = 1`) leaves how many rows?
questions.why: One row per company. For JPMorgan, the 22 Oct Program Manager application wins.
